title: Quarantine late usage adjustments and ensure idempotent export lines
creator: Jordan Liu
description:
Problem summary: Late-arriving usage events (rate-limit refunds, delayed webhook retries, and retried meter reports) are being applied directly to invoice export lines, which causes duplicate or conflicting Stripe/NetSuite invoice lines when backfills land. This manifests as: duplicated credits, invoices that don't net to zero when expected, and customer confusion. Root causes observed: (1) exporter writes lines immediately without a quarantine window or tentative status; (2) idempotency keys are insufficiently scoped (missing source+window+adjustment-type), so retries create new lines; (3) backfill and live pipelines use slightly different rounding rules leading to micro-differences that prevent de-duplication.

Goal: Introduce a quarantine stage and tentative export line flag, strengthen idempotency keys, and harmonize rounding rules so late usage adjustments are held and reconciled before being exported. This will reduce duplicate invoice line creation, make exports idempotent across retries, and improve invoice accuracy for mid-cycle adjustments.
tasks: Add 'quarantine' lifecycle: store late adjustment records in billing_quarantine table with reason and source metadata
Define 'tentative' export line schema: add tentative boolean and provenance_token to export payloads
Compute robust idempotency key: sha256(customer_id + adjustment_type + window_start + window_end + source_event_id)
Update exporter to dedupe by idempotency key and tentative flag before creating Stripe/NetSuite lines
Backfill: run reconciliation job to sweep existing near-duplicate lines and mark eligible ones as tentative or merge when safe
Harmonize rounding: use shared rounding util to 6-decimal intermediate precision then round to cents for exports
Add metrics: duplicate_export_attempts, quarantine_queue_size, tentative_line_observed_count, quarantine_resolution_time
Feature flag the quarantine/export changes for gradual rollout per-customer tier
acceptance_criteria: Late usage events (arriving >1hr after original window) are inserted into billing_quarantine and not immediately exported
Duplicate export attempts reduce by >=95% in canary accounts compared to baseline over 7 days
Exporter rejects creation of Stripe/NetSuite line if idempotency key already exists (idempotent behavior verified with simulated retries)
Backfilled duplicates are either merged or marked tentative and reconciled before final export
QA verifies cents-level totals match expected after harmonized rounding for a sample of 500 rows
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency key generation covering edge cases (missing source_event_id, DST boundaries, negative adjustments)
Integration test: simulated pipeline that emits duplicate late events and validates single export line creation
Staging e2e with Stripe sandbox: exercise retries, webhook re-delivery, and confirm no duplicate invoice line items
NetSuite sandbox run: validate that tentative lines are created as memo entries and only finalized after reconciliation
Load test: process 10k simultaneous late adjustments to verify exporter throughput and quarantine queue behavior
production_rollout: Deploy behind 'billing_quarantine' feature flag. Phase 1: internal canary accounts (2). Phase 2: 10% of production customers with high rate-limit usage. Phase 3: global. Monitor duplicate_export_attempts and quarantine_resolution_time SLOs; rollback on >3% duplicate regressions or exporter error rate >0.5%.
